q: Do I need to enable test-signing mode?
a: No. Standard profiles use UMDF2 with a locally trusted certificate. The bundled USB/IP kernel packages retain their upstream Microsoft signatures. The SDK does not enable Windows test-signing mode.

Composite Sony and Valve profiles install the bundled usbip-win2 0.9.7.5 transport on a machine that has none. Standard profiles use the Windows UMDF2 stack. A machine with a working usbip-win2 keeps the one it has, so there is nothing to do when updating.

q: Can I add a controller you don't ship?
a: Yes, without touching code. Write a data-only JSON profile, or point HMDeviceExtractor at a controller you have plugged in and get a ready-to-deploy profile back.

q: How is this different from ViGEmBus, vJoy, or VIIPER?
a: Those tools install kernel drivers and present a small set of fixed device types. HIDMaestro runs in user mode and presents the exact identity of the profile you pick, 231 of them, down to the bus type, and adding a device means writing JSON rather than driver code. VIIPER additionally routes input through a network stack even for local play. The full comparison table above puts the tools side by side.
